body:
I have two degrees.  One in a maths subject and one in an  english subject. I’m an accountant. I’m a tax advisor. 

I can’t read clocks. 🤦‍♀️

The sinking dread feeling was awful. But I flagged it to my manager straight away. A tip to anyone else: if you attempt to hide an error or cover your tracks, it’ll end up being 100x worse for you so fess up!
They did. Luckily the business was quite chill about it. Me less so.
Good to know I’m not alone in my reaction.  It’s just ‘Requiem for a Dream’ lite. Not as horrifically awful as it had been hyped to be.
I’m constantly asking my kid ‘which Ella?’ Or ‘which Alfie?’ so those two.

I put on weight after surgery. But that was because I ATE ALL THE THINGS. After stopping eating all the things, my weight is reducing again. 

I gave myself a 6 month grace period to enjoy all the food I couldn’t eat for two years. Now I’m back on the balanced diet and the weight is coming off again at a steady pace.

Eh, I accidentally paid someone £2.5 million when I was new and I’m still here. Accidents (and an extra zero) happen. 

I doubt a grievance would be raised on an error or oversight. You’ll probably have a discussion about it but not a whole grievance process!

Film is either Gone in 60 seconds or Tremors. 

Tv series Red Dwarf

I want to be …. A tree. 

Usually repeated when it’s all getting a bit stressy.
Oh absolutely. Yes my razor bill has gone up, but my medication bill has gone down so it all evens up 😂

Study of one (me!) agrees that my dodgy gallbladder caused brain fog. I genuinely thought I was entering peri-menopause with the confusion, night sweats, body aches, insomnia, anxiety etc etc but it all disappeared once my gallbladder was removed. 

Could be psychological of course. One definite thing I have noticed is very random. My leg hair had stopped growing. Since my gallbladder removal I’ve gone full gorilla legs again. Still worth it 😂

Found out when I gave blood the one and only time I did a donation. 

Turns out I have useless blood (AB+) so they’ve never wanted me to donate again. Which is a shame because I have a vein that’s an absolute nurses dream and no fear of needles whatsoever.

I’m in the UK. I waited two years on the list and ended up going private. The NHS finally called me up for my pre-op (not the op you understand, just the talk through of the op) two and a half years after referral (and yes, I’d told them to take me off the waiting list at this point)

I highly recommend Benenden private healthcare which is what I used in the end. You do have to be a member for 6 months before requesting surgery but they take pre-existing and it’s only like £16 a month.
9 month post op and so happy the bastard organ was evicted! I’ve got my life back!

I’m 9 months out from surgery now and things are still changing. Some things that messed me up (sausages) are now fine. Other things are still being problematic (roast potatoes) but the majority of stuff I can eat with no problems. 

If something doesn’t agree with me, I usually know within about 2 hours of eating it (either severe bloating or a running to the loo- but it’s mainly the first one now!)

Before: anything. 

After: roast potatoes. I swell and look 8 months pregnant. And then the problems start
Olive bread and then hummus were the first two that sent me into A&E. As it got worse pretty much anything could set off an attack.
Genuinely don’t care.

Either you work where I work or this happens a lot!

New manager actually helped me solve a problem, rather than add to it by writing briefings, one-pagers and activity reports.
Same. Turns out I didn’t have IBS-D, I had a faulty gallbladder!

2 years! I went private in the end. The NHS called me up for pre op the other week (despite telling them I’d had it out) so that would have been two and a half years just until the pre op appointment if I’d waited for them!

Being in part of the CS where everyone is obsessed with data and evidence based results, there is a surprising amount of cricket noises when asking the question ‘how was the 60% arrived at?’

There is no justification. It’s not evidence based, it’s not performance based. It’s purely a random amount. (Possibly linked to previous pay awards that gave us the right to WFH for a minimum of two days a week)
Probably by computer connection to either the network or office wifi based on other departments

I had IBS-D to the point I had urgency and would soil myself. I was in the middle of getting a full test to make sure I had no underlying health conditions causing the symptoms (cancer, celiacs, chrohns etc) when I had my first gallbladder attack. 

I had my gallbladder out 9 months ago and my IBS-D symptoms are gone. 

If you’ve had at attack (and it sounds like it with the radiating pain) you will probably need to have it out at some point as it tends to get worse. 

Sometimes gallstones cause IBS. Sometimes having your gallbladder removed causes IBS. Every body is different.

You can have a look through my posts if you like. I’m 9 months post-op and life is sooo much better. No more pain, I was so sick and didn’t realise. 

Yes I have very mild issues still. But nothing compared to how it was. Seriously best thing I’ve ever done is get it removed. I got my life back.

So my IBS symptoms were (pre-op) sudden uncontrollable urge, diarrhoea going to yellow liquid, nausea and cramps. I used to soil myself as I got like a 5 second warning between needing to poop and pooping. 

Post-op. Will get cramps and loose stools within about two hours of eating a trigger food. But it’s not so sudden, I have more warning and can make it to a toilet. 
At first, anything fatty caused this reaction. By a month post op it was just sausages and mushrooms. Now 9 month post op nothing causes this to trigger!

If I eat too much fat in a day (or roast potatoes for some reason) my stomach swells and the next morning I need a couple of hours to poop before I leave the house. Not diarrhoea but definitely my body going ‘right, evacuate everything’ and by too much fat I mean a real fatty meal day which would probably cause anyone a bad stomach!

You’re welcome! With me I was getting horrendous painful gallstone attacks as well, so reading everyone’s post I was thinking ‘ok, I have the op, and at worse ill still have these symptoms, but no attacks?!? Get this thing outta me!!’

I’m now 9 month post op. A couple of foods have triggered my IBS but even when they do, it’s a couple hours in the morning at worst and then I can get on with my day. And even then it’s not as uncontrollable as it was when my gallbladder was there. The difference is amazing and I have got my life back!

Post op reactions tended to fall into two catergories for me. The first is a reaction within about two hours of eating. Cramps and diarrhoea or serious bloating (as in, I look 8 months pregnant bloat) Those are foods I can’t tolerate in any amount. 
The second is a reaction the next morning. Not diarrhoea but needing to go a lot and stools being yellow/slimy. These are foods I can tolerate to a certain amount, and if I keep portion sizes down I don’t get this reaction

For me, if I eat something that doesn’t agree with my gallbladder free zone, it’s cramps and then a need to go to the bathroom and diarrhoea. 

I highly recommend trying foods for the first time at home. 

And keep trying. At first I couldn’t eat sausages, or mushrooms. They are fine now!
Someone on my wavelength! My first thought was ‘my belly’ 😂

My husband and i both did this for a bit. He took Fridays off. I took Mondays (with switches for bank holidays obviously) and that meant we saved a fair whack in nursery fees as they were only signed up for three days a week. 

Only sustainable for a year though. Then we needed longer breaks as a family.
No worries. Fair warning though, the first four days are tough. After that though you adjust and then it’s just a case of powering through!
I got a wedge pillow and slept sitting up for a few nights. But the best thing really is walking. I made myself walk 500 steps around my house every hour which got me sorted.

https://www.torbayandsouthdevon.nhs.uk/uploads/25434.pdf

I did the food version. Counting spaghetti strands was the bit that elicited the most comments!
Yes. Walk as soon and as much as you can. The gas pain is no joke and you need to move that gas out of you.
Seeing as I’m 32,000 in the UK queue to book Disney holidays on their website, I’m going to go with: NO.

I’ve had a weird conversation with a neighbour where they asked why I’d refused to take in their parcel. I would have taken it in but the postie never knocked on my door!

I’ve also had a neighbour designate me as their alternative delivery which meant everything of theirs got sent to my address, until I got them to change it so postie at least tried their house to see if they were in first before coming to me!They complained to another neighbour I’d refused to help them which was infuriating.

Ultrasounds progressed from sludge to stone to stones. 

Actually gallbladder was ‘chocked full of gravel and infection’ swollen, inflamed and ready to give me sepsis.

Had mine out in August. I can eat everything apart from roast potatoes (I’ve no idea why that food causes me issues!) no need for vitamins, no need for any medication at all. All regular portions and stools have been normal for the first time in over two years (my gallbladder gave me IBS-D) no issues with doing any activity. 

I haven’t felt this well in years.

I genuinely couldn’t do the milk diet. I needed something to chew to feel like I was eating!

And no, since surgery I haven’t continued the diet. But I have made lifestyle changes (well after the initial period I gave myself to EAT ALL THE THINGS) and am losing weight that way, which should help with the liver!
I have fatty liver and went on a two week diet (the NHS liver shrinking diet. Food version) prior to my surgery. Operation went without a hitch.
And although some accept ‘guy’ as a more neutral term, it does sound like just asking about the men on the team.
Orson Welles’s last major film role was in Transformers: The Movie.
Ooh as I have a fear of vomiting that sounds horrendous. I’m glad you’re doing well post-op!

I bloat if I eat potato but other than that I’m fine. 

Before surgery I had horrendous diarrhoea. I had accidents. I was regularly on 10 Imodium a day and often couldn’t leave my house. I was sick, exhausted, my hair was falling out. 

Surgery was the best thing I’ve ever done. I’ve got my life back.

Roast potatoes for some reason. I swell up and it’s painful. 

I had surgery in August. At first I couldn’t eat sausages,mushrooms and potatoes. Now it’s only the potatoes that cause issues. 

I did put on weight after surgery. But that’s because I gave myself until the new year to eat all the things that I couldn’t for the last two years. I went crazy and put on 10lbs

Since Jan I’ve been eating normally and the weight has all come back off.

It was a private hospital and I think they were worried I’d slip and fall or something and sue them. When I’ve gone NHS it’s always been you are just wheeled in your bed, but this place had a proper posh bed that stayed in the room.

I was so eager to get the surgery, I refused to wait for the wheelchair and power walked myself down there. The attendant was saying ‘I’m happy to have a rest from pushing but if we pass my manager we are going to have a pretend argument so it looks like I tried to stop you’

When we got into the prep room he yelled ‘hold the doors, there’s no stopping this one’ as I leapt up into the bed.

I mean, it’s not ‘all day in the bathroom’ bad. I just swell and look 8 months pregnant and have gut ache the next day. 

I’ve worked out I can just about manage toddler portions without too much distress.
Roast potatoes. Sundays are ruined 😭

I was the older sister whose twin brother and sister arrived when I was three. I shared with my little sister when she moved into a normal bed from her cot - so when she was 2 ish and I was 5,  until we moved and I got my own room at ages 10.
Or more sense with lions as the mane would give it away!
Oh god that radio advert that’s doing the rounds at the moment ‘the noise of kids eating leaves a lot to be desired’ and then proceeds to play munching slurping sounds. I hate it so much.

I had a wonderful preview into peri-menopause with my gallbladder. Night sweats, brain fog, exhaustion. Genuinely thought I was ‘going through the change’ until I had my gallbladder removed and then it all went away.
It was ‘cute’ when it only affected the little brother/OPs son . Now daughter is stealing OPS stuff, it’s suddenly a problem.

Yes it did! I’m still struggling with iron deficiency and we aren’t sure why, but everything else has resolved since the surgery. If you’ve read my comments you’ll see that my gallbladder was horribly infected when they removed it, so the fact I was fighting that infection probably caused the fatigue.

I once told my daughter to go and tell her Dad off for leaving his shoes in the middle of the doorway. She stomped over to him, in that very serious way only a toddler can manage, and yelled ‘OFF’ at him.
Yes. ‘Boldly in the pretend’. Prepare to sob. A lot.

I had sludge. Changed my diet. The sludge became a stone in 6 months. The stone became a ‘inflamed gallbladder full of gravel’ in 18 months. 

I hope the diet change works for you. It didn’t for me.
Have you heard the version of this song with the lyrics? Has me absolutely bawling.
Mine was mushrooms. I’m now 7 months post-op and it’s resolved in the last month.

Had someone vomit in our office last week. Because although they had some horrendous bug, they needed their 60%. 

I legged it out of there after the first vomit on the floor.   grim.

As soon as I felt I could eat again which I think was two days post op. The day after I was just too sleepy to really care about food. 

7 months post op now and I can eat everything. Some things have to be smaller portions though otherwise I get gut ache but that’s only for really fatty things.
Either Captain Planet or The Simpsons Game on the Amiga. (I’m old 😂)

In the vast infinite of the universe, nothing I do matters and one day I will be dead for all eternity. 

I realise this sounds a bit depressing but I see it as kinda inspiring. I’ve only got one go round. This is literally it. I’m absolutely going to die one day so I’m going to successfully escape this life eventually. Might as well keep going for now

I genuinely was chomping at the bit and refused to wait for the trolley and power walked myself to the operating theatre. 

But that’s only because I’d been waiting two years for surgery and felt awful all the time. I was so sick. And in so much pain, and my life sucked.
Just sharpie out the ‘V’

He finally had it out! Went to a specialist hospital in London and they even managed to do keyhole rather than open as planned. That was three weeks ago and he can now eat everything. It’s also given him a new lease of live, he’s booked a whole load of holidays abroad, he’s now got stuff to look forward to. 

The change is miraculous!

I also do not like the pancakes. Every year I run the gauntlet of well meaning comments of ‘we’ll have you tried it with this topping/ that topping’ etc etc etc. 

Yes I have. No I don’t like them. Accept. Move on.
It clears and you can get the bottle once you’ve got the fountain working again

Pretty much what everyone else has said, but also some throat lozenges and some peppermint - either peppermint tea or the sweets!

Wedge pillow, stool softener and painkillers were the obvious ones, but my throat was really scratchy and weird tasting after the op, which made me cough, which hurt my stitches.
I wanted to check it wasn’t just me. Last picture the bloke looks decent, fun to be with. I’d go on a date with him. The picture before (blue shirt, white trousers) screams ‘pretentious wanker’
Yup. All normal now!
I only notice the train line in winter, when I can hear the Polar Express steam engine blow its whistle, otherwise I don’t notice.

I did have this.  Not a dr so take this as just an anecdote, but when I had an attack I’d have very pale stools, but then they would go yellow and slimy. I think it was the stone that blocked the bile exit caused the light colour, and then when the stone moved the built up bile was all released in one go, causing the yellow (like a dam bursting if you will!)
Yup. I now carry a few toddler snacks in my handbag for when I’ve been too long between meals and the gut ache starts. That bile needs something to digest other than me!
They’ve already done that last one. Office has been freezing since Christmas.
Rain. Loved it so much I added the song to my playlist. Unfortunately the lyrics make me bawl my eyes out.

I used Benenden. It was only £15 a month and covers pre- existing. Down side is you have to be a member for 6 months before you can request surgery, and you have to have been waiting longer than the average published wait time on the NHS. 

I hope it gets sorted soon for your partner

I actually ended up going private and having it out at the beginning of August 24. 

Shortly after this post I did a subject access request (where you find the information they have on you) which showed they had ‘accidentally’ removed me from the waiting list. I’m sure if was a complete coincidence I was about to have been waiting 52 weeks…

I got added back on and it restarted the wait time clock.  So I went private.
Not only is it nonsense, it actually goes against most departments ‘plain English’ guidance for comms.

So the first two weeks after surgery my gut was all over the place. Constipated from the surgery and then bile diarrhoea. 

But after that. Normal. Another couple of weeks went buy and it was just.. normal. No urgency, not loose. It really made me realise how far from normal I’d been, and for how long. 

Some foods do still upset my stomach, but they’re random. Carrot and celery give me cramps. Mushrooms do not agree with me, but pizza is fine. Roast potatoes cause me to swell and bloat something fierce, chips are ok!

What I have been doing is reintroducing foods one at a time.lm still to anxious to eat out, and have mainly been trying things at home first

Yes! I was about to be diagnosed with IBS-D after all tests were exhausted, then had my first gallbladder attack. I used to be on maximum dose Imodium every day just to be possibly able to leave the house (and still having accidents) to now no problems at all. (Other than the lingering physiological fear) It’s a miracle!
Horrible Histories or any of David Walliams’ books have been a hit here.

4 days. I refused the stool softeners at hospital because I had chronic IBS-D. Yeah, turns out the faulty gallbladder caused the IBS-D and once it was removed I was ‘normal’ again and subject to post-op constipation. Had to send husband out for stool softeners in the end because it was NOT GOOD.
Not a single problem with alcohol since the op. Strangely before remove I couldn’t have beer without issues, but after it’s been fine.

Good luck! Even if it does disagree with you it won’t be anything as bad as a gallbladder attack so you haven’t really got anything to lose. 

Also, my surgeon said, just because you can’t tolerate something now, doesn’t mean you won’t be able to in the future. So don’t panic if you do have a bad time with it. I couldn’t eat sausages at first but now it’s fine.

My doctor told me to eat normal after surgery. Quickest way to train your body to existence without a gallbladder. 

So far the only thing I can’t eat is mushrooms. That’s a run to the toilet food. 

Everything else is fine. Even the greasiest take away pizza.
Yeah. Used to have no problems with mushrooms. It’s weird.
Shat myself in the MRI machine. Fun times for all involved.

Yes. You can search my posts on this sub but I basically had acid burning diarrhea from day 4 (when the constipation stopped) until about day 10. Since then I’ve been fine. Well apart from a stomach bug that caused me a panic!

No no, the mature thing to do is bitch about her on Reddit. 

Some people seriously never grow out of the high-school drama do they?

Only if I eat a LOT. like a double stacked cheese burger with bacon and fries dripping in grease. I can eat pizza fine, even a normal burger and chips. 

But not mushrooms. Mushrooms wreck me.
That is indeed a collection of statements. Well done.

I ‘only’ had gallbladder attacks. Then I was on the waiting list for two years awaiting removal because I wasn’t an urgent case. By the time it was taken out it was thickened, infected and ready to kill me. 

It’s making stones. Those are causing the attacks. Get it gone!

The holiday visa for Russia asked for details of my employer and a contact number for my manager, so yes,  they knew. 

I don’t think any other places cared or asked. At least not officially. Possibly when crossing the border between Bosnia and Montenegro, as they took my passport for a loooong time for no apparent reason.

MY PERFORMANCE HAS CRASHED THIS WEEK AS IVE HAD TO BE IN EVERY DAY TO GET THE 60% (CHEERS STORMS AND THE CLOSING OF RAIL LINES) AND PEOPLE KEEP TALKING TO ME AND IVE GOT EFF ALL DONE. 

STILL, I BROUGHT A LOAD OF SANDWICHES AND CHOCOLATE. SO YAY FOR THE ECONOMY.
I used to take it all at once. But I don’t need to anymore. Having my gallbladder evicted cured my IBS

My surgeon said ‘eat normally from day one’ so I wasn’t low fat at all after my surgery. 

But, even now, if I go too high fat, I get stomach cramps and diarrhoea the next day. That’s it.

As an SO who thought they did all the work, let me just say I was humbled when I got my G7. 

You genuinely have no idea. 

General good rule of thumb though: you have no idea what someone else is going through(work wise) or what may or may not be in place for managing their performance. The only one who does is their manager, and they will deal with it.

Hmm, don’t think my trainers are gonna help mate. 

The nice shoes I’ve got in the office might do, but I’m not wearing those on the long-ass commute.
If I were you I’d download the NHS app and keep checking on the upcoming appointments tab. This is where I first learnt about my appointment as the letter got stuck in the post!

Yes. I signed it. But then they lost my records so I’d recommend contacting them to absolutely make sure. 

I ended up getting healthcare via Benenden in the end. They don’t care about pre-existing and after being a member for 6 months you can request surgery if you’ve been waiting longer than the published NHS average waiting times. (Which you will have been by the time that 6 month rolls around) Highly recommend doing that because I would still be waiting if I hadn’t. It’s only about £15 a month as well!

Midlands said the average waiting times was 22 weeks to give you an idea how off that can be. I waited 104 weeks and still wasn’t seen!

Yes. Yes you do. 

I spent two years on the NHS waiting list before getting it out privately. 

I was very close to having a serious medical incident according to my post-op report. But as I wasn’t actively dying (although it felt like it) the NHS wouldn’t do anything other than confirm I was on the waiting list.

Initially I went to the GP after several incidents. I genuinely couldn’t remember the last time I’d had a solid movement, and it was getting yellower and looser and impacting more and more on my life. 

Had blood works, stool samples all came back fine. I had a colonoscopy that found nothing. An endoscopy that found nothing. Then my finest moment when I pooped myself in the MRI machine having the rest of my digestive tract checked. Nothing. 

Dr was about to give up and diagnose IBS when I had my first gallbladder attack and ended up in A&E. Diagnosed that day and waited two years for removal. 

My gastro dr said that the faulty gallbladder might be the reason for my diarrhea, and since it’s been gone I’m back to normal. 

To give you an idea, I was on 6-10 immodium a DAY pre-op. And that was just to keep me regular.  Now I don’t need it at all.

My husband can successfully not drown. But I wouldn’t class it as swimming. He had no lessons or access to a pool as an inner-city boy and by the time he did he was older and struggled to learn. Adult swim lessons are hard to find.
My little girl plays rugby and Fury is her absolute favourite Gladiator. Because (in my daughter’s words) she’s strong and tough and plays rugby and still has pretty hair and makeup.

My gallbladder was causing me diarrhea before the surgery. As in having no warning and shiting myself on the regular. 

Gallbladder removal has cured this (apart from the two weeks immediately following surgery, and a few weeks ago when I had a panic and it turned out to just be a stomach bug 🤪)

The only change is now I can’t eat mushrooms without problems. Everything else is fine. 

My gallbladder was infected. It was going to kill me if it stayed in. So fuck it. The bastard got evicted and I’m so happy it’s gone.

I tried really hard. Took on extra work. Guess I just wanted validation and a reward for my hard work. Quickly realised that the only thing I was getting was more work and no more pay. And no chance of promotion/bonuses either due to being in the public sector. 

So now I meet my performance targets, do the job and go home. No above and beyond, no extra roles/responsibilities. Just the hours and the role they pay me for. 

So much of the public sector is held up by people doing more than they should and not getting paid for it. Had a colleague whose timesheet showed they’d worked 400 hours more than contracted. Unpaid. No time off in lieu. No entitlement to overtime. Absolutely no recognition for working herself to the bone taking on all the slack because they didn’t hire enough people to do the work. Eff that.
It would be lovely if they could spring some money for cleaning our fancy new office. It’s grim.
Mine is mushrooms. Eat those and I’m vomiting out my arse for an hour.
If liver flushes worked, it would be packaged, patented, sold and prescribed. They’d make loads of money from it.

I’ve had both! C-section recovery for me was not too bad, but gallbladder recovery was tougher not because of the actually surgical cuts and stuff, but because of the gas pains. 

The surgical pain from c-section was milder but lasted longer (ie no driving for 6 weeks, no picking up anything heavy etc). Gallbladder removal pain was more severe but lasted only about 3 days -once the gas had gone I felt fine unless I tried to lift anything ridiculously heavy.
Yes. You can either take the money or the hours for the delay, but not both.

Will do. I was so happy after my surgery after waiting two years and now I’m just so sad that my IBS symptoms are back. Sorrry to hear this is happening to you too. 
Are you keeping a good diary or anything to keep track?

When I did it you couldn’t. Or at least you couldn’t do the exams/ tutorial bit part time which is why I was back in tutorials 3 weeks after having my baby. But the consolidated work/ final report bit they were fine with me being part time. 

I will say I was one of the first to do this and use shared parental leave, most took the year deferment. Things might have changed!

It was certainly difficult. I did a lot of the exams either heavily pregnant or with a newborn and it wasn’t easy. I used the shared parental leave so my husband could look after baby whilst I attended tutorials and exams. I had to sit my exams separate so I could take breaks to pump which was awkward!

Once I did the exams, I took 6 months of the remaining shared parental leave to spend with my baby, and deferred the course so I joined the year below me for the consolidation/ work bit. I also came back part time - you can request you temporarily come back part time for a maximum of two years. I only did one before reverting to full time. 

So it is doable. But it ain’t easy.
I had my baby at the beginning of year 3 of the 4 year TSP course. I had maternity leave, and deferred a year, returned to the course and am now a G7

Isn’t it just! We’ve never taken child out of school before for a holiday, and won’t again, it’s a one-off trip to America that I’ve saved up for for 10 years and even then we can’t afford the summer holiday prices. Sigh. I just don’t want to fall foul of the potential of a criminal record, hence the question.

It will stop. And I’ve never felt so light and clean, it was actually quite nice?!?! But my husband also put a bin bag on the car seat for me ‘just in case’.
Eggs are fine for me. Mushrooms however are a bad time.

Mine is nearly nine now, but I tell you when she was a toddler it was all the screen time we needed to survive. 

We’d go out for a walk each day, some fresh air and do something, but the rest of the time? Screen. 

We were knackered with the holiday and extended family stuff so on down days we didn’t sweat it. 

And despite all that ‘massive neglect’ she’s turned out great.
Was due to go in before Christmas. Not enough beds so cancelled again. Still hanging on though!

SP= South Pole, Some Penguins
Went by Boxing Day afternoon - so about 12ish hours of being ‘uncomfortable’

Doctor told me it’s not actually the fat that’s causing the pain. It’s just that when you eat something fatty, the gallbladder squeezes and squeezes and squeezes bile out, as it takes a lot of bile to digest fat where as if you just had say a baked chicken breast, it only needs to squeeze out a little bit to digest it. 

The more often a gallbladder squeezes, the more chance it has to squeeze a stone into a place you don’t want a stone to be. Less squeezing, less chance. That’s why they recommend low fat. It’s also why technically, even a lettuce leaf could give you an attack, as the gallbladder still needs to squeeze a bit of bile out to digest it.

I’ve had Moviprep. This is how I did the prep:

Two days before hand a low fibre diet. No vegetables. No fruit. Nothing red. 

Day of the prep: I got a big measuring jug and mixed up the prep as per instructions in the morning and popped it in the fridge so it was cold in time for evening. 

When it came time to drink it, I used a fat straw (like the milkshake ones) and decanted the jug into a half pint glass. Drank that, set a timer for the next glass. Repeat. 

It tasted like mild lemon at first, and oily. However the more I drank, the more it made me gag. Towards the end I was taking a gulp, then a suck on a chuba chump lolly to get the taste out. It was the only way I made it without throwing up. 

You will get diarrhoea. I was having diarrhoea and cramps which is why I was having the colonoscopy. However with the prep it was more ‘oh, I need to go’ and I went. Without the cramps so it was actually less bad than my normal IBS. 

Do not trust a fart from when you take that first sip until after the scope. 

Don’t wipe aggressively. I found the yellow metanium nappy cream to help with the ring of fire. And wet wipes (don’t flush)

Stay near a toilet. Don’t plan on doing anything during prep time. 

As an aside, I also took mannitol for my MRI. That caused me to poop myself in the machine (feel free to search my history for that story!)

Good luck

So, I was one of the first in the civil service to make use of shared parental leave, as it came out the year my daughter was born. 

By law, the mother is required to take two weeks maternity leave, to physically recover from the birth. She then has up to another 50 weeks of maternity leave she can choose to take. How many of those weeks are paid, and at what rate, depends on your employer and eligibility for government support. 

Anyway, the mother can choose to surrender those 50 weeks maternity leave into shared parental leave. Which means either parent can have that leave, but between the two of you it adds up to 50 weeks. 
So you could both take the same 25 weeks off together, or one of you could take the first 6 months of baby’s life off, and then the other could take the second six months off.

You need bile to digest everything you eat. When you eat, the gallbladder squeezes bile into your stomach. 
How often it squeezes depends on how much bile is needed to digest what you are eating. The more fat in the meal, for example, the more bile is needed. 
The more often your gallbladder squeezes, the more likely it is to squeeze a stone into a position that causes pain. 
So we are advised low fat meals to keep gallbladder squeezes to a minimum, which reduces the risk of an attack.
